title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Low-Resource Languages: A Comparative Study of LLMs for Bengali Hate Speech Detection
measurement_description: The paper measures the performance of fine-tuned large language models in detecting Bengali hate speech. As part of this evaluation, the study utilizes a dataset (BD-SHS) where 'Religious Hate' is a specific subcategory (comprising 9% of the dataset's hate speech samples) to evaluate the models' ability to detect online abuse, including religious intimidation.
findings: The models were successfully fine-tuned to detect Bengali hate speech, which encompasses 'Religious Hate' (4,521 samples in the dataset). Llama-3.2-3B achieved the highest overall F1-score of 92.23%. While religious hate speech was successfully categorized as part of the broader hate speech detection task, the paper does not isolate or report model performance metrics specifically on the religious hate subcategory.
